verses.text: Seven women shall take hold of one man in that day, saying, “We will eat our own bread, and wear our own clothing: only let us be called by your name. Take away our reproach.”
In that day, Yahweh’s branch will be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land will be the beauty and glory of the survivors of Israel.
It will happen, that he who is left in Zion, and he who remains in Jerusalem, shall be called holy, even everyone who is written among the living in Jerusalem;
when the Lord shall have washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion, and shall have purged the blood of Jerusalem from within it, by the spirit of justice, and by the spirit of burning.
Yahweh will create over the whole habitation of Mount Zion, and over her assemblies, a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night; for over all the glory will be a canopy.
There will be a pavilion for a shade in the daytime from the heat, and for a refuge and for a shelter from storm and from rain.

footnotes.content: A strange comfort, isn't it? When the men are gone and the city lies broken, these seven women ask only to be claimed and covered by a name. They've lost so much already—husbands, sons, status. What they want now is to belong to someone, to stop being unseen. The Lord hears the cry of the forgotten.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Yahweh's branch'—this is the language of a living thing growing toward light. After judgment comes life: beauty, glory, and the fruit of the land restored. The remnant will see what a merciful God brings forth. In Christ, we see that Branch made flesh.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Written among the living—what a phrase. It speaks of a roll kept in heaven, a record that marks who belongs to the Lord. The survivors of Jerusalem will be called holy not because they earned it, but because they're inscribed in His book. Grace writes our names there.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The filth and blood must be washed away by justice and by fire—both judgment and purification at once. The Lord doesn't leave His city in shame. He cleanses it. He restores it. Every stain is seen and addressed by His eye and His hand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mount Zion wrapped in cloud and fire—the very signs of God's presence in the wilderness and at Sinai. The 'canopy' is protection and glory both. Where God dwells, His people are shielded. The sign of His dwelling is their security.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo: the storms still come—hardship, loss, the heat of sorrow—yet many of us have found that the Lord's covering holds. A pavilion for shade, a shelter. Not escape, but presence in the midst of it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
